name: ensemble_signal_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: No single strategy works in all market conditions. By running 4 distinct sub-strategies simultaneously — VWAP mean-reversion, EMA crossover trend, Bollinger breakout, and RSI reversal — and entering only when >= 3 of 4 agree on direction, we create a robust ensemble signal. Each sub-strategy captures a different market microstructure (reversion, trend, breakout, exhaustion), and their errors are partially uncorrelated. The inefficiency persists because building and maintaining multiple concurrent sub-strategies requires significant engineering effort. The ensemble's edge comes not from any single signal being novel, but from the diversification benefit of combining them.
mechanism: Multiple independent signals confirming the same direction increase the probability that a genuine order flow imbalance exists, not just noise. When momentum, volume, and volatility signals align, it indicates that institutional activity is creating measurable market impact across multiple dimensions simultaneously, increasing the confidence of directional prediction.

conditions: close > VWAP OR Ensemble_Score == 4 (override VWAP filter if full consensus)

exit.signal_exit: Ensemble_Score crosses zero (majority flips against position)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; halve size if VIX > 20

weaknesses: Sub-strategies are correlated — VWAP reversion and RSI reversal often agree, while EMA crossover and BB breakout often agree; effective diversification is less than 4 independent signals
The ensemble can produce conflicting signals between mean-reversion (Sub1, Sub4) and trend-following (Sub2, Sub3), creating a structural tension; 3/4 consensus rarely occurs
Target/stop ratio of 40/20 = 2.0 with 61% win rate seems optimistic; slippage and the tight 20 bps stop will cause many premature stop-outs in volatile 1-min bars
prior_art: Ensemble methods in ML (Random Forest voting); Elder's Triple Screen; combining mean-reversion and momentum signals discussed in Chan (2013) 'Algorithmic Trading'
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
